mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota C-HR PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota C-HR PHEV (M20A-FXS) engine replacement typically costs £3,200-£4,200 for a rebuilt unit, £2,800-£3,500 for reconditioned, and £1,200-£2,200 for a used engine. Supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,200 depending on the specialist and your location. Rebuilt engines include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Used engines are the cheapest option but carry higher risk. The 13.6kWh battery is a separate component - replacement costs £3,000-£5,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Toyota C-HR PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include rough idling, increased fuel consumption, engine warning light illumination, hesitation on acceleration, and poor cold start performance. Early M20A-FXS units have seen reports of faulty direct injectors. Injector replacement costs £1,200-£1,800 at specialist rates. Delaying repair can cause cylinder or piston damage. Regular servicing and fuel system cleaning can help prevent issues.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota C-HR PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2024-2025 C-HR PHEV is valued between £17,625 and £30,470. With a rebuilt engine costing £3,200-£4,200, replacement is usually worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise in good condition. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. Rebuilt engines come with a 12-month warranty for peace of mind. The Toyota Relax warranty can cover up to 10 years if serviced at a main dealer.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota C-HR PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement on a Toyota C-HR PHEV takes 2-3 working days for supply and fit through a specialist. Used engines may be available faster if already in stock; rebuilt engines typically require longer lead times. Most specialists offer next-day or 48-hour delivery on used units. Rebuilt engines typically require 5-7 working days. The hybrid system calibration adds time compared to a conventional engine swap.

mainEntity.name: What engine code does the Toyota C-HR PHEV use?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Toyota C-HR PHEV uses the M20A-FXS engine code - a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine from Toyota's Dynamic Force family. It is paired with a 161bhp electric motor and a 13.6kWh battery to produce 220bhp system output. M20A-FXS is the sole engine code for the C-HR PHEV. Always verify your engine code using your V5C registration document. The engine is transversely mounted with e-CVT transmission.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a Toyota C-HR PHEV replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: All engines supplied through EnginesMarket carry a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Toyota's official Relax warranty can cover up to 10 years if the vehicle is serviced at an authorised Toyota dealership. 12-month warranty covers parts and labour on rebuilt engines. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier. Warranty transfer options may be available depending on the supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota C-HR PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota C-HR PHEV was introduced to the UK market in March 2024, completing the electrified powertrain line-up for the second-generation C-HR. Positioned as the performance-oriented plug-in hybrid flagship, it pairs a 2.0-litre Dynamic Force petrol engine with a powerful electric motor to deliver 220bhp - the most potent powertrain ever offered in a C-HR.

milestones.description: Second-generation Toyota C-HR unveiled; PHEV variant announced as flagship model
2024 (March) - C-HR PHEV goes on sale in the UK from £39,145 in Design, Excel and GR Sport trims
2024 onwards - M20A-FXS 2.0-litre plug-in hybrid remains the sole PHEV powertrain across the range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota C-HR PHEV is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota C-HR PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Toyota C-HR PHEV's M20A-FXS plug-in hybrid powertrain is broadly robust, drawing on Toyota's proven hybrid expertise. However, as a relatively new model, certain issues have begun to emerge - particularly around direct injector reliability and hybrid battery degradation. Rebuilt M20A-FXS engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Direct Injector Failure - Why the Toyota C-HR PHEV M20A-FXS Suffers Fuel System Issues
problems.rootCause: Early reports indicate a batch of faulty direct fuel injectors in some 2.0-litre hybrid power units, causing rough running, increased fuel consumption, and potential engine damage if left unaddressed.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four direct injectors, recalibrate ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before significant engine damage
Best if injector failure has caused cylinder or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2024-2025 Toyota C-HR PHEV is valued between £17,625 and £30,470 used. With the vehicle firmly in the £17,000-£30,000 bracket, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine replacement usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For higher-mileage examples approaching the lower end of this band, evaluate both options carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you catch injector issues early (rough idle, increased fuel consumption, engine warning light), the injector replacement route offers significantly better value than a full engine swap. If the engine has suffered collateral damage, a rebuilt M20A-FXS with upgraded components is the sensible long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M20A-FXS Toyota C-HR PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation - Why the Toyota C-HR PHEV Loses EV Range Over Time
problems.rootCause: The 13.6kWh lithium-ion battery pack in the C-HR PHEV naturally degrades over time and charge cycles, reducing electric-only range from the original 41-mile maximum.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace degraded cells or modules only
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one or two modules are failing
Best if battery has significant capacity loss across multiple modules
Only if battery failure has caused wider powertrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - a typical C-HR PHEV sits in the £17,000-£30,000 bracket. For a vehicle in this range, battery replacement often makes financial sense, particularly with the warranty protection against future failure.
problems.recommendation: Battery degradation is inevitable on any plug-in hybrid. If diagnosed early (reduced EV range, frequent engine starts), cell/module replacement is the right call. If the battery has significant capacity loss across multiple modules, a full pack replacement offers better long-term value. The engine itself rarely needs replacement due to battery issues alone.
